audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gives Swain Level 6, the first item and two items, while its own whys[4], whys[5] and whys[6] say Malphite is too tanky to burst at 6, that his first armour item makes the shield nearly unbreakable, and that a full-tank Malphite cannot be killed by Swain alone.
audit.why: The mirror's read is that early lane is Swain's on range, Levels 4-5 even out, and from the first item Malphite is favoured. The packet agrees from Level 4 onward.

audit.whatIsWrong: early says Vision of Empire 'roots him briefly'; mid calls Unstoppable Force 'a point-and-click stun' and says 'your E cannot interrupt' it; whys[1] describes rooting him 'for the passive pull'. Ground Slam's armour scaling and Granite Shield's size are absent.
audit.why: Riot text: Vision of Empire damages, slows and reveals, and grants a Soul Fragment on champion hit — the root is Nevermove, and it roots on the RETURN sweep, after which Swain recasts to pull. Unstoppable Force is a 130/115/100s leap to a location that knocks enemies up; it is not point-and-click and not a stun, and there is no channel on Demonic Ascension for it to interrupt. Ground Slam is 7s flat and its damage scales off his Armor. Granite Shield absorbs up to 10% of his max health and recharges when he goes unhit.
audit.corrected: Slot roles and all four numbers written into early, mid, whys[1], breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, dosFull[0].d and phases[4].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page frames his armour purely as defence you route around with magic damage.
audit.why: Ground Slam's damage scales off his Armor, so every armour item he buys is also an offensive buy — that is why the trades get worse for you faster than the resistance numbers suggest. Thunderclap also applies on-hit, so his damage scales with attack speed too.
audit.corrected: Armour-scaling written into breakdown.cooldowns and phases[5].why.

edits.after: Unstoppable Force knocks you up from 1000 units — it does not stop Demonic Ascension, but it starts the fight on his terms. Block the angle.

edits.after: Unstoppable Force is 130s and knocks you up from 1000 units — it does not cancel your drain. Fight after it.

edits.before: With E now available you can root him in place for the passive pull before he ever reaches you; he has only a slow in response and cannot stop the root-pull sequence.
edits.after: Nevermove roots him on its return sweep and you recast to drag him in; all he has in reply is a point-and-click slow, and that does not break the root.

edits.before: At level 1 Malphite has nothing but a point-and-click Q slow and his passive Granite Shield — he cannot punish your Q poke as long as you stand at max range and respect the shield before trading again. The moment he regenerates that shield (it refills when he avoids damage for a few seconds), poke it off with Q, then immediately step forward to land W before he can react: the demonic eye roots him briefly if it connects and lets you pull with passive. He has no answer to this at level 2, so chain W-into-E whenever his shield is down and walk away with two or three Soul Fragments banked before level 3.
edits.after: At level 1 Malphite has nothing but a point-and-click Q slow and his passive Granite Shield — he cannot punish your Q poke as long as you stand at max range and respect the shield before trading again. The moment he regenerates that shield (it refills when he avoids damage for a few seconds), poke it off with Q, then step forward and land W: the eye slows him and hands you a Soul Fragment, and the E root that sweeps back drags him in. He has no answer to this at level 2, so chain W-into-E whenever his shield is down and bank two or three Soul Fragments before level 3.

edits.before: Around levels 4-5 Malphite becomes genuinely hard to kill — he stacks armor passively and his Q slow starts to matter when you need to walk into range for E. He does not kill you either, but your W-E-Q combo starts doing less proportional damage as his resistances climb and his shield soaks the opener. Level 6 is the danger pivot: his R is a point-and-click stun from a massive range that he can use to one-shot engage onto you or your team, and it is an unstoppable dash that your E cannot interrupt. Play around the minion wave to block his R angle, use W proactively to zone him before he can coil for the dash, and avoid standing in the open near the edge of his R range (around 1000 units). Do not give him a free R by positioning carelessly.
edits.after: Around levels 4-5 Malphite becomes genuinely hard to kill — he stacks armor passively, Ground Slam's damage scales off that armor, and his Q slow starts to matter when you need to walk into range for E. He does not kill you either, but your W-E-Q combo does less as his resistances climb and Granite Shield soaks the opener. Level 6 is the danger pivot: Unstoppable Force is a 130s leap from about 1000 units that knocks you into the air, and it does not switch Demonic Ascension off — what it does is start the fight on his terms. Play around the minion wave to block his angle, use W proactively to zone him before he can coil for the dash, and avoid standing in the open near the edge of that range. Do not give him a free R by positioning carelessly.

notes: Two structural errors fixed: Vision of Empire was credited with the root (it slows and grants the Soul Fragment; Nevermove roots, and only on the return sweep), and Unstoppable Force was described as a point-and-click stun that your E cannot interrupt. It is a leap to a location that knocks up, and there is nothing on Demonic Ascension for it to interrupt — the mirror flagged five strings making that same claim on their side. Kept diffRating at 6/10 while diff moved to EVEN so the number stays consistent with breakdown.difficulty and report[14], which already read 6/10.
